subject: PO activation & invoice cadence — holdback and net terms discussion
messages:
From: Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@novacare.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PO activation / holdback / invoice cadence for Redwood deployment

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team is eager to move forward. Procurement has a few constraints we need to capture before issuing a formal PO:

- We require a single PO referencing the engagement (no multiple POs per month) and the PO must include the vendor tax ID and defined remit entity.
- Standard holdback: 5% of monthly invoice held until acceptance of delivery milestones per SOW.
- Net terms: our baseline is Net60 for new vendors; for pilots we can do Net30 after PO activation.
- Invoices should be issued weekly (itemized run-rate), but we need a consolidated monthly statement for payment processing.
- PO number must appear on each invoice line.

I've attached our PO template for your finance team (attachment: Novacare_PO_Template.pdf). Please confirm whether Redwood can meet these constraints or if we need an amendment to the SOW/contract.

Also, is there any preferred invoice metadata we should include to speed up ERP matching?

Appreciate a quick read — procurement needs this nailed down to approve the SOW.

Best,
Amelia Torres
Sr. Procurement Manager
Novacare Health
From: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: PO activation / holdback / invoice cadence for Redwood deployment

Vanessa / Karthik — forwarding Novacare's PO template and ask below. Key asks: single PO, 5% holdback, weekly invoices + monthly statement, Net60 baseline but pilot Net30. They want PO number on each line and vendor tax ID on PO.

Can finance/legal confirm:
- Accept 5% holdback on monthly run-rate or require a different structure (e.g., cap the holdback to first invoice)?
- Weekly invoice cadence with consolidated monthly statement: will this break our billing automation / collections SLA?
- Net terms: any recommended compromise between Net30 pilot / Net60 enterprise?

I attached their PO template (Novacare_PO_Template.pdf). I can push a short amendment if needed, but want to avoid slowing the close. Need an answer today if possible — procurement is on a tight timeline.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
From: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
To: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: PO activation / holdback / invoice cadence for Redwood deployment

Jonas — quick guidance from billing/procurement ops: 

- Holdback: we can accept a holdback but recommend capping it to 3% and limiting it to the first full invoice (one-cycle holdback). A rolling 5% holdback each month creates reconciliation overhead and increases DSO risk.
- Weekly invoices + consolidated monthly statement: acceptable. We'll need the weekly invoice file to include: PO number, invoice line item SKU mapping, billing entity, and a reference to the monthly statement ID. Our AR automation supports weekly items if they roll up to a single monthly settlement.
- Net terms: propose Net45 standard. For the pilot, we can do Net30 for the first 30 days post-activation, then Net45 thereafter. Net60 materially increases cash conversion concerns for smaller vendor teams.
- PO metadata: ensure PO number, remit entity, vendor tax id, and a short SKU mapping (we'll provide a billing guide).

I'll attach our internal acceptance checklist (Redwood_PO_Acceptance_Guide.pdf). If Novacare insists on 5% ongoing holdback and Net60 only, we should treat it as a contract amendment and request additional underwriting.

Karthik, happy to hand off any legal wording changes; if you prefer, I can propose a terse amendment for signature (DocuSign).

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Billing Operations
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
From: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
To: Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@novacare.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@novacare.com>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: PO activation / holdback / invoice cadence for Redwood deployment

Amelia — thanks for the clear ask and the PO template. Short answers and our preferred compromise below so procurement can proceed: 

1) Holdback: we can accept a holdback but request a capped approach — 3% of the first full invoice only (not a recurring monthly deduction). This keeps reconciliation light and aligns incentives for initial acceptance.

2) Invoice cadence: we can support weekly, itemized invoices as requested. Please include the PO number and SKU line mapping on each weekly invoice. Redwood will produce a consolidated monthly statement (statement ID included on each weekly invoice) so your AP can process a single monthly payment.

3) Net terms: for the pilot we can do Net30 from PO activation; for ongoing enterprise purchase we propose Net45 standard. If Novacare requires Net60 for the full term, we will need an underwriting approval and a short amendment to the agreement.

4) Required PO metadata: please ensure PO includes vendor tax ID, remit entity, and PO number visible on each invoice line. Our AR team also asks for a short SKU-to-service mapping field to avoid ERP mismatches — sample mapping attached (Redwood_PO_Acceptance_Guide.pdf).

If that works, I can share a one-paragraph amendment for signature (DocuSign link) to capture the holdback cap and pilot terms, or we can proceed with your PO and include the amendment post-activation. Which do you prefer?

Next steps: 
- If procurement confirms the capped 3% first-invoice holdback + weekly invoices + pilot Net30 then we can accept the PO as-is and begin onboarding.
- If Novacare insists on recurring 5% holdback or Net60 for the pilot, we'll need signature on a short amendment and underwriting sign-off.

Thanks — I'll standby for your direction.

Best regards,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Attachments: Redwood_PO_Acceptance_Guide.pdf
